newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait, AGIP deal said worth about $500 mln.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait, AGIP deal said worth about $500 mln.

text.p: Kuwait's deal with Agip SpA for a 50 percent share in the Italian firm's Milazzo refinery and purchase of 330 filling stations could be worth $500 million, industry experts said on Thursday.
"The deal is worth about $500 million but it is a complicated contract and the price includes a two-stage upgrade scheme for the refinery," said an expert close to Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC).

KPC said on Tuesday its subsidiary, Kuwait Petroleum Italy, had signed a deal for the stake in the refinery and acquiring 330 Agip filling stations in Italy with an annual throughput of about 500 million litres (110 million imperial gallons) -- 1.5 percent of the Italian retail market.

KPC did not give a value for the deal but said in a statement, "The implementation of such an agreement is subject to the approval of (Italy's) Antitrust Authority which started examining this deal a few months ago."
It said the deal also provides for the upgrading of the refinery in Sicily to produce higher quality products and become more competitive.
Experts said the refinery has a current output of 220,000- 240,000 barrels per day but the two sides plan to upgrade it to process high sulphur sour crudes similar to Kuwaiti crudes.
"The upgrade involves deep conversion and desulphurisation units to be able to run on sour crudes to meet local (Italian) market requirements," said an expert familiar with the deal.

It allows KPC to "reenter the Italian oil refinery industry and will expand its retail activity in Italy," said KPC, which closed its refinery in Naples in 1993 and has since been trying to re-enter the market in southern Europe.
The deal would raise output from Kuwait's share in European refineries to about 250,000 bpd. KPC's only other oversees refinery is in Rotterdam, with a capacity of 80,000 bpd.
KPC said in August it would close its uncompetitive 59,000 bpd refinery in Denmark early next year.
